correctness.rationale: For arbitrary integer p>=2, selected/excluded neighbor distances are disjoint integer multiples of 1/(2^p-1), proved by parity and separate treatment of the smallest numerator. Hence the specified symmetric open intervals select precisely the intended lone stubborn opinion at each orbit point, strictly away from switching boundaries. The actual SCOD averaging map sends u_j to u_{j+1} and the last point to u_0; all u_j are distinct. A neighborhood follows the same itinerary, contracting exactly by 2^-p each period. Exhausting two-agent trust configurations proves minimality. Exact rational finite checks p=2..40 and 312 perturbed laps passed; this is supportive, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The original source explicitly asks when two distinct stubborn opinions can produce oscillations; period length and attraction are natural dynamical invariants. A complete any-period existence theorem for a fixed minimal agent count disproves any agent-count-only upper bound on periods. Open basins and parameter robustness distinguish durable cycles from a single fragile explicit orbit; the rational finite-union construction makes the condition reproducible. It does not pretend to be a global attractor classification.
